status: structural prototype; not authorized for provider use
scope_statement: These items establish deterministic semantics, scoring, schedule identity, and counterbalancing structure only. They do not establish that any item is unsaturated, discriminating, or appropriately difficult for a frontier model.

model_visible_interface.selection_template: You are selecting a requested configuration for the task described below. Choose one displayed option. This records a request only. Any task execution and configuration assignment are controlled separately by the task runner; this interface does not guarantee that the requested option will be assigned or that a task run will follow. Return exactly PLAN:<LABEL> with no other text.
model_visible_interface.option_template_work_score: <LABEL> — up to {max_answer_slots} answer slots; at most {score_cap} points; no tools.
model_visible_interface.option_template_tool_budget: <LABEL> — up to {max_answer_slots} answer slots; at most {max_tool_calls} calls to {tool_name}; at most {score_cap} points.
model_visible_interface.execution_template: Task configuration: {configuration_description}. Complete only the enabled slots. Return one line per enabled slot as <SLOT_ID>=<ANSWER>.
model_visible_interface.semantic_identity_rule: The same byte-identical selection template, option renderer, task description, and response parser must be used in every execution arm. Only the displayed counterbalance variant, item payload, and configuration values supplied by the frozen assignment record may vary.
forbidden_extra_cues: explanations of why a configuration occurred

response_parser.semantic_parser_policy: Trim leading and trailing ASCII whitespace only, then apply the strict pattern. No synonym, prose, or inferred-intent recovery is permitted in v0.
response_parser.canonical_recode: Use the selected presentation variant's displayed_label_to_canonical map.

task_response_parser.record_rule: After ASCII line-ending normalization, require exactly one nonempty line for every enabled slot and no other lines. Line order is ignored after parsing.
task_response_parser.identifier_rule: Every identifier must belong to the enabled-slot set and must occur exactly once; an unknown, disabled, missing, or duplicate identifier makes the task response semantically invalid.
task_response_parser.value_rule: Pass the captured non-whitespace value to the pair-specific scorer normalization and exact answer-key comparison.
task_response_parser.freeze_rule: The parser and all pair-specific normalization rules must be frozen before any model response is opened.

presentation_counterbalance_v1.allocation_rule: Within every pair x dose cell, allocate the four variants equally before any responses exist. Canonical recoding occurs only after parsing the displayed label.

shared_scoring_rules.enabled_slots_only: Only slots enabled by the assigned schedule are presented and scored. Disabled slots are absent and cannot earn points.
shared_scoring_rules.score_formula: One point for each enabled slot whose normalized answer exactly equals its answer-key value; total score is capped at the assigned score_cap.
shared_scoring_rules.missing_or_extra_output: A missing enabled slot earns zero for that slot. An unknown or duplicate slot identifier makes the task response semantically invalid. Extra prose makes it strict-format invalid.
shared_scoring_rules.no_post_treatment_matching: Scores, errors, tool use, and completed work are realized outcomes; none is used to rematch schedules or establish assigned-schedule identity.

schedule_application_rule: A pair-level active or zero-dose schedule selects slot ordinals from the phase-specific payload. Active schedules are used for the executed baseline payload. Follow-up schedules and answer keys are retained to establish matched structural semantics, but the primary protocol records the follow-up configuration choice without executing that payload in the same session.
payload_disjointness_definition: Disjoint means that no problem-instance identifier or instance-specific input is reused between a pair's baseline and follow-up payloads. The task rule, renderer, scorer type, and option semantics are intentionally shared so that the two phases remain members of the same item family.
